title: Say it another way
cards: When I was at school, we memorised lots of dates.
Back in my day, we learned lots of dates by heart.
DAY
Most of what we did had nothing to do with real life.
Most of it was completely out of touch with real life.
TOUCH
At my kids' school, they learn by doing things themselves.
My kids' school is very hands-on.
HANDS
We spent months on those dates, and it was all for nothing.
It was a complete waste of time.
WASTE
I use my Latin surprisingly often.
I use it more often than you'd think.
THINK
It might be useful one day. Who knows?
You never know when it might come in handy.
HANDY
((Software does a lot of the drawing.)) The thinking is the part where I'm really useful.
The thinking — that's where I really add value.
VALUE
((My law degree?)) I haven't needed it once in all these years.
I've never used it since.
SINCE
((In the new country,)) my degree and my experience didn't matter.
None of it counted.
COUNTED
I had to begin all over again, from nothing.
I had to start from scratch.
SCRATCH
Retraining took a lot of effort, but in the end it was worth it.
It was hard, but it paid off.
PAID
A course helps, but only up to a point.
A course only gets you so far.
FAR
My grandmother can still say dozens of poems from memory.
My grandmother learned dozens of poems by heart.
HEART
We had to figure out how to read contracts on our own.
Nobody ever taught us how to read a contract.
TAUGHT
Why do we even learn Latin? It's useless.
What's the point of Latin?
POINT
((You don't need a course for that.)) You learn it as you go.
You pick it up along the way.
PICK

speaking: Each of you: three things you learned at school — one that **came in handy**, one that was **a complete waste of time**, one **you've never used since**. Whose school was more useful?
"**Back in my day** …" Each of you: two ways school was different then. Agree on the one change that was for the better.
Think of someone who had to **start from scratch** — you, a friend, someone you've heard of. Tell the story in five sentences, with two phrases from the box. Your partner asks two questions.
"**It was hard, but it paid off.**" Each of you: two things that were hard to learn but **paid off**. Agree which one paid off most.
Which card was the hardest? Each of you: two new sentences with it about your own school or work.
hint: Think together. Take turns to say it another way, with the word in red — the others agree or not. Then tap the card to check.
